Foreign-Backed Sabotage Disrupts Italian Fisheries Industry

Italy’s fisheries industry is facing major disruption following a series of coordinated sabotage incidents against processing plants and coastal facilities, which authorities have attributed to a foreign state seeking to undermine the sector. The attacks, which began late Monday, targeted sites in Liguria and Sicily belonging to several leading firms, including MareVivo Italia and Azzurra Pesca.

According to Italy’s Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries, at least seven major facilities have experienced forced shutdowns due to deliberate equipment damage and the disabling of on-site cold storage systems. “The scale and precision of these attacks indicate a high level of technical knowledge and planning,” said Deputy Minister Marco Gentile, adding that investigations are ongoing.

Hundreds of fisheries workers have been sent home on temporary leave, with unions warning of mounting uncertainty should the incidents persist. “Our members are deeply concerned for their livelihoods and safety,” said Elisabetta Romano, spokesperson for the National Fisheries Workers’ Union. “We urge all stakeholders to prioritize the protection of our industry and its people.”

Industry analysts estimate that up to 30% of Italy’s fisheries processing capacity is currently offline, with daily losses for affected firms potentially exceeding €3 million. The Italian Fisheries Association described the situation as “unprecedented,” citing not only the immediate production losses but also long-term reputational risks for Italy’s seafood exports.

Security measures have been stepped up at all major fisheries sites nationwide, with some facilities operating at reduced capacity amid heightened alert. As authorities work to restore full operations, the sector remains on edge, bracing for further disruptions in the days ahead.
